translation.english_title: Like the jewel of the eye

english_lines: Lallala lallallaa,
Like the jewel of the eye,
Like the seed of a fruit,
We sons of the soil, among ourselves —
Why bitterness and hatred?
For the sons of the soil to live — in this
Soil, is there no right?
The duty is to guard the eye —
Is that such a great trouble for the eyelid?
If one walks forsaking duty,
What is guarding for? Tell me, ayya.
(Like the jewel of the eye).
notes: `மண்ணின் மைந்தர்` remains `sons of the soil`, keeping the political-social belonging language concrete.
The eye/eyelid duty image is kept literally rather than turned into abstract civic prose.
The closing colloquial `சொல்லையா` retains its spoken address as `tell me, ayya`.

english_lines: To climb the sky and leap across the sea,
Courage is needed; wisdom is needed even more,
To climb the sky and leap across the sea,
Courage is needed; wisdom is needed even more,
We must see unity in difference,
The feeling of enmity must fall by the roots,
Let us give a hand for kinship; let us give voice for rights,
Say `naam` — we — and see,
The lips meet; relationships bloom,
Say `naan` — I — and see,
The lips do not join; the relationship too does not part,
(Like the jewel of the eye).
notes: The repeated sky/sea and courage/wisdom lines remain repeated.
`உறவுக்கு கை / உரிமைக்கு குரல்` keeps the established `hand for kinship / voice for rights` architecture.

`நாம் / நான்` is kept as `naam / naan` so the lip-position wordplay remains visible. The verified closing `பிரிவாது` produces a semantically awkward contrast and is translated conservatively rather than repaired.

translator_notes: The song moves from belonging and civic duty into unity/rights rhetoric and a phonetic `naam / naan` argument; the English keeps all three registers visible.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
